newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic power falls before holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic power falls before holiday weekend.

text.p: Expectations of easing demand in the Mid-Atlantic over the President's Day holiday weekend pushed lower spot bulk electricity prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool.
The price drop for short-term power was cushioned by forecast of below-normal temperatures in the region Sunday and Monday, market sources said Friday.
"The two things were working against each other, the holiday and the coldest days of the week being Monday and Tuesday," said a Houston-based power trader.
Many participants, who planned not to work Monday, traded Monday and Tuesday PJM power as two-day blocks.
Firm, peak PJM electricity prices for Monday and Tuesday (excluding transmission costs) changed hands at $25.25-26.25 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Thursday's $26.50-27.00 for delivery today.
PJM power prices for firm, off-peak delivery for the two days remained at $18.00-20.00, while PJM cost through Tuesday for off-peak generation continued to hold near $15.50.
Pool operator lifted its "split system" status for the PJM network over the three-day holiday weekend with a projection drop in energy and transmission demand, market sources said.
Day-ahead transmission capacity in the grid was tight for more than a week due to high power flows into the eastern part of the system.

Peak, next-hour dispatch rates in the western part of the grid will stay at $25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) level through Monday, then leaping to $33.00 Tuesday. Rates in the east will ease down to $31.40 during the long weekend, and return to today's level of $38.70 Tuesday.

Dispatch rates in the east are much higher because utilities have fired up expensive oil and natural gas plants to balance the grid, enabling them to bring in cheap, coal-fired generation from the west.
PJM power for delivery Monday to Friday was quoted near $25.00, compared with Thursday's $25.25-25.75. PJM deliveries for Wednesday through Friday were assessed at a range of $24.25-25.50.
Quotes for PJM power for the remainder of February widened to $24.75-26.00 from $25.50-26.00 Thursday.
March PJM power prices were better bid at $23.85-24.00, compared with Thursday's $23.80-24.00.
PJM prices for April and May stayed at $21.80-22.00, while June PJM power remained at $24.75-24.90.
July/August PJM electricity widened to $29.30-29.60 from Thursday's $29.45-29.55.
PJM third-quarter deliveries remained at $27.55-27.75, and fourth-quarter PJM prices softened to $23.45-23.70 from $23.60-23.80 Thursday. Firm, peak 1998 PJM deliveries were still pegged near $25.80.
Separately, swing natural gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate today slipped further to $2.50-$2.70 per million British thermal units, down 20-30 cents from Thursday.
NYMEX Henry Hub gas futures rebounded from Thursday's loss on shortcovering. At 1343 EST, the March contract was up 4.1 cents at $2.040/mmBtu.
